rules.whyItMatters: The rate on the notice must be the sum of the experience, social and EAF rates, applied for the whole year.
rules.effective: ESD's tax rate page; the rate sent each December applies to the entire next calendar year.
rules.excerpt: We send your tax rate each year in December. It applies to the entire next calendar year. ... Your total tax rate: experience tax rate + social tax rate + EAF. ... The fee ranges from 0.02% to .03%, depending on your rate class.
matchPhrases: we send your tax rate each year in december. it applies to the entire next calendar year
your total tax rate: experience tax rate + social tax rate + eaf
the fee ranges from 0.02% to .03%, depending on your rate class
rules.pageOrSection: About unemployment tax rates; Your tax rate
rules.ruleOrLimit: Total rate = experience rate + social rate + the employment administration fund (EAF) fee, 0.02% to 0.03% by rate class. The December notice sets the rate for the whole next year.
rules.hangsApplication: The client's 2026 rate notice, dated December 12, 2025, assigns rate class 20: experience 2.38% + social 0.70% + EAF 0.02% = 3.10%, for all of 2026. Applied to Q3 taxable wages: $1,247,822.40 x 3.10% = $38,682.49.

rules.question: Why is the EAF 0.02% for this employer and not 0.03%?
rules.whyItMatters: The EAF is part of the total rate; rate class 20 is exempt from the additional 0.01% that most classes pay.
rules.effective: RCW 50.24.014 as published, last amended by 2026 c 268 s 931.
rules.excerpt: (1)(a) ... Contributions to this account shall accrue and become payable by each employer, except ... at a basic rate of two one-hundredths of one percent. ... (b) ... Contributions to this account shall accrue and become payable by each employer, except ... those qualified employers assigned rate class 20 or rate class 40, as applicable, under RCW 50.29.025, at a basic rate of one one-hundredth of one percent. ... (2)(a) Contributions under this section ... shall not be deducted, in whole or in part, from the remuneration of individuals in the employ of the employer.
matchPhrases: at a basic rate of two one-hundredths of one percent
those qualified employers assigned rate class 20 or rate class 40
at a basic rate of one one-hundredth of one percent
shall not be deducted, in whole or in part, from the remuneration of individuals in the employ of the employer
rules.ruleOrLimit: Each employer, with the statute's exceptions, pays 0.02% under (1)(a). The additional 0.01% under (1)(b) does not apply to qualified employers in rate class 20 or 40. These contributions may not be deducted from employees' pay.
rules.hangsApplication: HANGS General Contracting is in rate class 20, so the EAF is 0.02%: 3.08% + 0.02% = 3.10%, not 3.11%. The Q3 register's deductions are 401(k), Section 125, federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, Additional Medicare, Paid Leave, WA Cares and L&I; no unemployment tax is taken from pay.

rules.question: What must each employee's line on the report show?
rules.whyItMatters: The wage detail is what ESD checks benefit claims against; a missing item makes the report incomplete.
rules.effective: WAC 192-310-010 as published; last amended by WSR 23-22-076, effective November 26, 2023.
rules.excerpt: (a) Tax report. Each calendar quarter, every employer must file a tax report with the commissioner. The report must list the total wages paid to every employee during that quarter. (b) Report of employees' wages. ... This report must list each employee by full name, Social Security number, standard occupational classification code or job title, and total hours worked and wages paid during that quarter. ... These standard occupational categories are identified by a six-digit numerical code.
matchPhrases: the report must list the total wages paid to every employee during that quarter
this report must list each employee by full name, social security number, standard occupational classification code or job title, and total hours worked and wages paid during that quarter
these standard occupational categories are identified by a six-digit numerical code
rules.ruleOrLimit: The tax report gives the quarter's total wages paid; the report of employees' wages lists every employee by full name, Social Security number, SOC code or job title, hours worked and wages paid.

The lines add to the register's $2,681,087.98 and 45,681 hours. The draft shows each Social Security number by its last four digits only.
hangsFactsUsed: Employee roster (names, Social Security last four digits, job titles, hire and leave dates)

rules.question: Which hours are reported for hourly and for salaried employees?
rules.whyItMatters: ESD uses reported hours to decide benefit eligibility; hours must be whole numbers, and salaried employees need hours too.
rules.effective: ESD's quarterly report filing page, saved copy retrieved November 5, 2026.
rules.excerpt: When reporting hours, round up to the next whole number. We don't accept any fractions of hours. Salaried employees: Report the actual hours an employee worked. If you don't track hours, report 40 hours per week for full-time employees. ... Severance pay, bonuses, tips and gratuities: Report zero (0) hours.
matchPhrases: when reporting hours, round up to the next whole number. we don't accept any fractions of hours.
salaried employees report the actual hours an employee worked. if you don't track hours, report 40 hours per week for full-time employees.
severance pay, bonuses, tips and gratuities report zero (0) hours
rules.ruleOrLimit: Report actual hours worked, overtime included, rounded up to whole hours. Full-time salaried employees are reported at 40 hours a week when hours are not tracked. Bonuses are reported with zero hours.
rules.hangsApplication: The hours reported are the hours associated with the wages paid in the quarter. Hourly employees: the register's actual hours, overtime hour for hour: 68 employees, 32,241 hours, including 1,969 overtime hours. Salaried employees: the employer accounts say no hours are kept for salaried employees (superintendents keep a daily job log of the job worked each day), so 40 hours for each week a salaried employee worked on the quarter's six biweekly paychecks, 12 weeks, 80 a paycheck: 28 employees, 168 paychecks, 13,440 hours. Total 45,681 hours, all whole numbers. On the amended Q2 report, the June 26 bonuses add wages but no hours.
hangsFactsUsed: Employee roster pay type (hourly or salaried)
Employer accounts: salaried time records, no hours kept
rules.unresolved: The 40-hour figure rests on the client's statement that no salaried hours are kept; the superintendents' daily job logs show the job worked, not hours, and are not among the files. Counting the quarter's 13 calendar weeks instead of the 12 weeks on its paychecks would add 40 hours for each salaried employee; a person confirms the method.

rules.question: Does every employee line carry a SOC code ESD accepts?
rules.whyItMatters: A missing or invalid SOC code can bring a penalty; ESD takes only six-digit codes ending in 1 through 9.

rules.excerpt: Provide a SOC code or job title for each employee in your unemployment tax report to avoid a penalty. This requirement started with reports filed for Quarter 1 of 2024. ... The code will be 6 digits. ... Valid SOC codes do not end in a zero. ESD accepts only SOC codes that end in 1 through 9. ... You cannot change SOC codes once you file.

this requirement started with reports filed for quarter 1 of 2024
valid soc codes do not end in a zero. esd accepts only soc codes that end in 1 through 9

rules.ruleOrLimit: Each employee needs a SOC code or a job title. A SOC code is six digits and must end in 1 through 9; a filed code is corrected only on a later quarter's report.

No line needs a job title instead.

rules.question: Is Tomas Arvelo's concrete finishing work covered employment that belongs on this report?
rules.whyItMatters: Work that needs a contractor registration, done by an individual, is outside employment only if all seven conditions are met; otherwise its wages and hours belong on the report.
rules.excerpt: The term "employment" shall not include services which require registration under chapter 18.27 RCW or licensing under chapter 19.28 RCW rendered by an individual when: (1) The individual has been and will continue to be free from control or direction over the performance of the service, both under the contract of service and in fact; ... (5) ... and has registered for and received a unified business identifier number from the state of Washington; ... and (7) On the effective date of the contract of service, the individual has a valid contractor registration pursuant to chapter 18.27 RCW or an electrical contractor license pursuant to chapter 19.28 RCW.
matchPhrases: shall not include services which require registration under chapter 18.27 rcw or licensing under chapter 19.28 rcw rendered by an individual when
the individual has been and will continue to be free from control or direction over the performance of the service
has registered for and received a unified business identifier number from the state of washington
the individual has a valid contractor registration pursuant to chapter 18.27 rcw
rules.ruleOrLimit: Contractor work by an individual is excluded from employment only when all seven conditions hold, including freedom from control or direction (1), a Department of Revenue registration with a UBI number (5) and a valid contractor registration (7).
rules.hangsApplication: The labor vendor list shows Tomas Arvelo, an individual, billing concrete finishing by the hour at $42.00 at Tideflats Cold Storage under the HGC foreman: $21,168.00 for 504 hours in Q3, paid through accounts payable. No contractor registration and no UBI number are on file, conditions (7) and (5), and the foreman's direction bears on condition (1). The draft reports the payroll as recorded. If the work is covered employment, $21,168.00 of wages and 504 hours belong on this report: $656.21 of tax at 3.10%. The other four labor vendors are companies with contractor registrations and UBI numbers on file.
hangsFactsUsed: Q3 2026 labor vendors paid (Tomas Arvelo: registration, UBI and insurance none on file; 13 weekly payments)
rules.unresolved: Reason: two of the seven conditions are not on file and the work ran under the HGC foreman's direction; whether it is covered employment is a decision for a person (LABOR-01). Nothing is added to the draft.
